steps.prompt: Think of the last film you told a friend about. How did you sum it up in one sentence at the end?

cards.title: Back to the main point
cards.body: A conclusion opens by restating the thesis: the same claim or focus, in new words. It reminds the reader what the whole essay proved.

cards.title: Restate, don’t copy
cards.text:
Thesis: Our school should start a community garden because it teaches science, improves meals and brings students together.
Restated: A school garden would turn our lessons, our lunches and our friendships into something better.
cards.note: Same three reasons, new words and a new order.

cards.title: Avoid announcements
cards.body: “In conclusion, I have told you about gardens” says nothing. Skip the announcement and restate the claim itself. The essay map marks a copied thesis with a !.

prompts: Which restatement are you proudest of? Why?
What is the difference between restating and copying?
